findings.title: AFTER triggers can erase or duplicate required effects while transfer reports success
findings.location: vault.py:_write_one and transfer before transaction commit
findings.evidence: Independent after-trigger-round-3.json: all four valid transfer probes returned a receipt and committed a missing credit, missing receipt, missing audit, or duplicate audit. Existing triggers remained present.
findings.expected: Verify debit, credit, receipt and exactly one added audit row before commit; propagate storage failure and roll back all effects if final effects differ.
findings.repair_scope: Preserve original API/schema/rows/triggers and tenant isolation. Reproduce all four cases and add regression coverage; retain concurrency and replay behavior. Preserve benign rowid-relocating triggers: internal rowid identity is not part of the contract.

findings.requirement: Preserve existing audit rows and add exactly one expected audit row.
findings.evidence: audit-followup-round-2.json and audit-followup-round-3.json independently show success after an AFTER INSERT audit trigger rewrites another tenant history, or deletes its old row and adds a duplicate elsewhere while keeping counts unchanged. Persisted content changes; the original contract requires preservation.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify complete contracted audit contents and duplicate multiplicity against the prior contents plus exactly the expected row; rollback all changes on mismatch. Preserve existing schema and triggers.

findings.location: vault.py:preservation of existing receipts and unrelated accounts
findings.requirement: Preserve existing rows, confine transfers to the authenticated tenant, and retain exact-replay deduplication after reopening.
findings.evidence: Independent preservation-round-3.json confirms both original-contract failures on this candidate: deleted historical receipt permits double execution on replay; unrelated tenant balance changes also commit.
findings.suggested_fix: Enforce preservation of existing receipts and reject account changes outside the authorized source/target, retaining tenant-scoped reads and existing triggers. Roll back unexpected effects and add API/CLI coverage for preservation and subsequent replay.

timing: Discovered by reverse cross-regression after original independent PASS; repair deferred until the nine frozen initial trials finish to preserve their order.
